fixes.explanation: That's it, baker! Joshua sends these tribes home with one big assignment, and it isn't about the land or the loot. Moses the servant of the LORD gave them the call “to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commandments, to hold fast to Him…” Hold fast, like a baker gripping a hot tray and NOT letting go. Love first, and holding on tight right behind it.

That's right, baker! Ten chiefs, “…one family leader from each tribe of Israel, each the head of a family among the clans of Israel.” And Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, walks right alongside them. I think that's a serious group. When ten family heads show up at your door together, nobody's asking if you want to talk. They're telling you it's time to talk.

Good guess, since Phinehas is a priest, and the text does call him "son of Eleazar the priest." But for the ten, the verse says they were “…one family leader from each tribe of Israel, each the head of a family among the clans of Israel.” That's how the text describes them: a family leader from every tribe. Phinehas is the one the text names as a priest, and the ten ride along with him.

Not quite, baker, but I get why you'd wonder. They showed up ready for a fight, so you'd expect them to leave grumbling! But the text says that when Phinehas the priest and the chiefs heard what the descendants of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh had to say, “…they were satisfied.” They came in hot and walked out calm. I've never seen a cookie cool down that fast.
